title: Tokenizer gating and chat-template version locks for safer model onboarding
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Background: New and updated open models arrive with varying tokenizer behavior and optional chat template formats. During recent onboarding runs we observed subtle tokenization shifts that cause role delimiters to be misaligned and structured output to degrade for customers using pinned model versions. Goal: Add deterministic gating checks and a template-version-locking mechanism to the onboarding pipeline so that any tokenizer/template incompatibility is detected early, flagged with remediation guidance, and (where safe) auto-mapped to a compatible template variant.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Onboarding CI runs include a tokenizer-compatibility stage that passes/fails with human-friendly diffs; 2) When compatibility fails, the onboarding dashboard shows suggested template variant(s) and a minimal mapping patch; 3) The pipeline can optionally pin chat template version for a model in the catalog metadata; 4) Deployments using pinned versions will receive a warning if runtime fallback mapping is used; 5) Unit and integration tests for three divergent tokenization cases are added and green in CI.
implementation_plan: Phase A - Detection (this sprint): implement tokenizer-signature extractor that computes stable tokenization metrics (role-boundary token counts, subtoken splits for common delimiters, leading/trailing sentinel tokens). Add a CI step that compares signatures against a compatibility matrix. Phase B - Guidance and Auto-mapping: build a ruleset that suggests template variant transforms (escape sequences, role delimiter normalization) and generate a candidate patch. Phase C - Version Locking: add a \"template_version\" field to model catalog metadata and expose it through onboarding UI and catalog publish flow. Phase D - Runtime warnings and opt-in auto-mapping: expose a runtime flag to allow automatic mapping for legacy customers with audit logs. Phase E - Monitoring: add telemetry metrics for mapping usage, false positives, and onboarding friction.
risk_and_tradeoffs:
- False positives: the signature comparator may flag benign tokenizer differences. We'll mitigate with thresholding and a human-review gate.
- Auto-mapping correctness: aggressive auto-mapping may change customer outputs; default is to require opt-in with audit logs.
- Catalog surface complexity: pinning templates increases catalog metadata complexity; we will document UX and provide a guided migration path.
- Time cost: additional CI stages increase onboarding latency; run heavy checks asynchronously and allow faster dry-run with optional deep checks.
testing_strategy:
- Unit tests for tokenizer-signature extractor across three tokenizers (byte-pair variations, sentencepiece variants, and whitespace-based).
- Integration tests that run the onboarding harness against a shadow runtime using pinned templates and verify output equivalence for a curated prompt set.
- Add e2e test that simulates a model with role delimiter mismatch and validates the suggested mapping patch and human override flow.
- Test matrix included in GitHub Actions config (ref: .github/workflows/onboard-tokenizer.yml, PR #4289).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge detection + CI steps behind feature flag and run on all onboarding PRs for two weeks. 2) Enable guidance UI and API metadata write for internal catalog only; collect triage feedback. 3) Release template_version metadata to limited partners (beta). 4) After 4 weeks of stability promote to public catalog and add runtime warning feature in next runtime minor release. 5) Post-release: run migration job suggestions for existing catalog entries.
monitoring_and_success_metrics:
- Percentage of onboarding runs failing the tokenizer gate that are resolved by suggested mapping >= 70%.
- Reduction in customer-reported structured-output regressions post-onboarding by 50% within one release.
- Mean time-to-triage for tokenizer incompatibilities < 48 hours.
- Telemetry: mapping_applied_count, mapping_reverted_count, tokenizer_gate_failure_rate.
